title: Split deploy.sh, the last over-cap file in phone_focus_mode
objective: Take deploy.sh from 875 lines to under the repo's 250-line cap. It goes last by design: every enforcer split this session grew its two hardcoded file lists, so splitting it earlier would have left the 'add to BOTH lists' step pointing at a stale location.
acceptance_criteria: bash meta/scripts/check_file_length.sh --all lists NO file under phone_focus_mode/, finishing that directory.
The two hardcoded file lists stay in exact correspondence after being moved into different files, and each carries a comment saying where its counterpart now lives.
do_deploy, at 421 lines, is cut at the phase boundaries it already prints, so each phase is a named function rather than an arbitrary line range.
Any function that stops being verbatim must have its behaviour proven unchanged against the pre-split version.
shellcheck passes on each file individually, with no -x and no disable directive; a global written in one file and read in another must not leave either file assigning something it never reads.
deploy.sh still runs: it reaches its usage message, which requires the whole source chain and config.sh to resolve.
Every phone-side test suite still passes at its previous count.
out_of_scope: Deploying to the phone; there is no device in this session.
Changing what is deployed, in what order, or the conditional handling of config_secrets.sh (which is deliberately asymmetric between the two lists and was so before this change).

Writing a test harness for the deploy phases themselves: every one of them is an adb call against a real device, and a stub layer deep enough to be meaningful would model the phone rather than test the script.
verifier: timeout 30 bash phone_focus_mode/deploy.sh (expects the usage message), plus check_file_length.sh --all showing no phone_focus_mode entry, plus the two-list parity check, plus every phone test suite at its previous count, plus pre-commit run --files on the touched files.
